concerns.text: The plan proceeds with a *placeholder CSV* because no verified HEA dataset is available (see “Critical data‑availability note”). Training and evaluation on synthetic, unverified data cannot support the research claim about real high‑entropy alloy predictive power, violating construct validity.

Uncertainty is quantified only by ensemble variance from Random Forest / Gradient Boosting models (Phase 2‑3.1‑3.3). Tree‑ensemble variance is not a calibrated predictive uncertainty metric and may not reflect true model confidence in extrapolation, undermining Principle VI (Extrapolation Integrity).

The Hold‑out Known set is created via a *non‑random* stratified split by element‑pair groups (Phase 0‑0.5). This deterministic split can introduce systematic bias and does not guarantee that the hold‑out truly represents out‑of‑distribution data, threatening the validity of the extrapolation error assessment.

The True Novel generation uses the same placeholder data to build a “Local Proxy Index” (Phase 0‑0.6) and then filters candidates against it. Because the index is derived from the same synthetic source, any leakage or overlap (e.g., hash collisions) may not be fully eliminated, confounding the novelty criterion.

Success Criterion SC-001 (report the interpolation $R^{2}$ score from the 5‑fold cross‑validation) is not mentioned anywhere in the plan. The phase only lists CV execution and model training but does not specify that the interpolation $R^{2}$ must be measured and recorded.

Success Criterion SC-005 (validate the reliability metric by comparing the variance distribution of the top‑100 novel candidates to the lower percentile of the training set) is absent. The report generation step (2.6) lists top‑100 candidates and summary statistics but does not require the variance‑distribution comparison required by SC‑005.

Success Criterion SC-004 (measure total pipeline execution time ≤ 6 h and RAM ≤ 7 GB) is only stated as a performance goal; there is no explicit step in the plan that records or validates the overall runtime and memory usage against these limits.

The plan relies on a *placeholder CSV* bundled with the repository because no verified open‑source HEA thermodynamic dataset (Materials Project / AFLOW Parquet) is cited. This means FR‑001 (retrieve HEA thermodynamic data) cannot be satisfied with a real, appropriate dataset, so the study cannot answer its core research question about predictive power on genuine HEA data.
